text:
GitHub Copilot Projects entered public preview October 28: goals, context, agents, and reviewed results in one place.
Our earlier Tech Thursday CLI image-batch experiment showed why the brief matters. Try three image concepts against three visual constraints; review before production.
Follow Layer8Culture if you're building with AI.

GitHub Copilot Fusion: stop choosing models without defining the job.

Fusion became generally available October 28. It routes and orchestrates models for a task instead of making you pick a model for every step.

What it does: one model can solve the task directly; a draft can be checked and escalated; or another model can critique the draft before revision. Fusion chooses the pattern. You choose Standard, High, or Max effort.

Builder value: fewer manual model switches while you keep ownership of the acceptance criteria. A stronger effort level isn't a substitute for a clear brief.

Try this week:
Update your Copilot client. Select Fusion Standard. Use a small, non-sensitive sample repo and ask: 'Fix this bug. Add a test that fails before the fix and passes after it. Do not change unrelated behavior.' Run the test and inspect the diff. If the task needs more reasoning, compare High on the same task and check actual usage, not just the answer.

Fusion bills each model it uses at that model's rate; multiple steps are not one flat-price call. Organization model policies still apply.

The signal: AI is becoming a routed workflow. Your job is moving toward specifying, checking, and deciding what ships.

Save this for your next Copilot build.

text:
Copilot Fusion changes model selection. It doesn't change who checks the work.

GitHub's October 28 release lets Fusion route models and, when needed, use checks or a second model's critique before revision.

Useful for builders: you can spend less time switching models and more time describing what a good result looks like.

Try it on one small bug. Select Fusion Standard. Ask for a test that fails before the fix and passes afterward. Run it yourself and inspect the diff. If the task needs deeper reasoning, compare High against the same acceptance criteria.

That is the workflow shift worth learning: define the job, let the tools work, verify the output.

Follow @layer8culture for AI builds with a human standard.
